title: 1 A fast-acting 5 × 20 mm fuse in an inline holder on a base

sources.citation: The 1 A fast-acting 5 × 20 mm glass cartridge fuse, a common supplemental-protection class listed to UL 248-14. Typical published figures for the class, paraphrased (not one vendor's): a cold resistance of about 0.1 Ω and a nominal melting I²t of roughly 0.5 to 1 A²·s (0.7 A²·s is taken).

game-design inside UL 248-14's envelope for supplemental fuses (paraphrased): carries its rating, opens within an hour at 135 % and two minutes at 200 %. The fictional datasheet's band, tested: carries 110 %; 135 %: 1 s to 1 h; 200 %: 0.1 to 5 s; 1000 %: 1 to 20 ms. I_min of 1.2 × the rating, between 1 and 1.35 as the envelope requires.

game-design: a fast element taking 30 % of the steady temperature rise inside a slow body (end caps and holder) of 10 s time constant, the element's own time constant (0.151 s) following from the melting I²t (electrical-realism-reviewer's worked example). It gives about 12 s at 135 %, 0.9 s at 200 % and 7 ms at 1000 %, near published fast-acting curves.
game-design: an inline fuse holder on a 70 × 30 mm base, 30 mm tall, with a screw terminal at each end; not modelled on a product. Replacing the fuse in P2 means deleting it and placing a new one.
